text:
### Observed differences

- **Participation rose from about half of the cases to nearly all.** Before, A28, A30 and A31 each ran in about 97 of 200 traces (about 49%) and A32, A33 and A34 in about 103 of 200 (about 52%), always once per trace; in the later window, each of the six activities runs in about 197–199 of 200 traces (about 99%). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]

- **Two trios that were alternatives now run together.** Before, no trace contained activities from both trios: pairs such as A28–A32, A30–A33 and A31–A34 had zero co-occurrence, with about 49 in 100 traces containing only the A28/A30/A31 member and about 51 in 100 only the A32/A33/A34 member. In the later window, each cross-trio pair co-occurs in about 98 of 100 traces, and the A28/A30/A31 member always comes before the A32/A33/A34 member. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024]

- **Both trios sit between A25 and A26 in both windows.** A25 and A26 appear in every trace throughout. Before, A25 preceded the A28/A30/A31 member and A26 followed it in the roughly 49–52 of 100 traces that contained a trio, while about half of the traces had A25 with no trio member at all; in the later window, A25 is followed by the first trio and A26 preceded by the second trio in about 99 of 100 traces. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]

- **Internal order within each trio stays unfixed.** In both windows, members of a trio co-occur in both orders in near-equal shares (for example, A28 precedes A30 in about half of the co-occurring traces and follows it in about half); this does not change. [REL013, REL014, REL018, REL025, REL026, REL027]

- **Routing follows the same pattern.** Before, A25's outgoing edges spread evenly over both trios (about 15–19% each); in the later window they go almost only to A28, A30 and A31 (about 30–38% each, with A32/A33/A34 at about 1%). Before, A28, A30 and A31 each led directly to A26 in about a third of their outgoing edges; in the later window these direct edges are marginal (about 0.5% for A28) or no longer observed for A30 and A31, replaced by edges into the second trio. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]

- **Positions and gaps shift as if a block was inserted.** The mean relative position of A28/A30/A31 moves earlier (about 0.74 to about 0.68) and of A32/A33/A34 later (about 0.73 to about 0.77); A25 moves slightly earlier (about 0.67 to 0.62) and A26 slightly later (about 0.80 to 0.83). The gap from A25 to A32/A33/A34, and from A28/A30/A31 to A26, is 1–3 steps in all before-window observations but 4–5 steps in about 98 of 100 after-window cases. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that two activity groups which were previously mutually exclusive alternatives became jointly executed in almost every case: before, each trace contained either the group A28, A30, A31 or the group A32, A33, A34 (about half of the cases each), placed between A25 and A26; in the later window, nearly every trace contains both groups in sequence — A25, then A28/A30/A31 in varying internal order, then A32/A33/A34 in varying internal order, then A26. [REL015, REL019, REL022, OCC001, OCC004, DIR001]

Supporting signs: the change is shown directly by relational evidence — cross-group co-occurrence rises from zero to about 98 in 100 traces with a fixed between-group order — and by participation rising from about half to nearly all traces; routing and gap evidence agree, with A25 now leading only into the first group, direct edges from the first group to A26 disappearing, and both flanking gaps growing from 1–3 to 4–5 steps. In total, 51 evidence items qualified against roughly 0.6 expected by chance for the 118 tested units, so the pattern as a whole is not what an unchanged process typically produces. [REL015, OCC001, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001]

Limitations: with 200 traces per window it cannot be excluded that traces containing both groups existed before as a variant too rare to appear in the earlier sample, or that the later window draws on a different case mix; the evidence also cannot show whether the second group is executed unconditionally or under a condition in the few later traces that lack it. [REL015, REL019, REL022]
